Q: Compiling OpenCV on Ubuntu with C++ version 17 A:

You can install OpenCV from Ubuntu's OpenCV package via the following:

For Python:

sudo apt-get install python3-opencv

For package libopencv-dev:

sudo apt-get install libopencv-dev

If you want to compile it and not use Ubuntu's OpenCV package, do the following:

# Dependencies
sudo apt-get install cmake
sudo apt-get install gcc g++

# For Python 2 support
sudo apt-get install python-dev python-numpy

# For Python 3 support
sudo apt-get install python3-dev python3-numpy

# GTK support
sudo apt-get install libavcodec-dev libavformat-dev libswscale-dev
sudo apt-get install libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev libgstreamer1.0-dev

# GTK 2 support
sudo apt-get install libgtk2.0-dev

# GTK 3 support
sudo apt-get install libgtk-3-dev

# Optional dependencies
sudo apt-get install libpng-dev
sudo apt-get install libjpeg-dev
sudo apt-get install libopenexr-dev
sudo apt-get install libtiff-dev
sudo apt-get install libwebp-dev

Now that you are done with dependencies, continue to the actual installation:

sudo apt-get install git
git clone https://github.com/opencv/opencv.git
mkdir build
cd build/
cmake ../

If properly configured, this is the output:

--   Python 2:
--     Interpreter:                 /usr/bin/python2.7 (ver 2.7.6)
--     Libraries:                   /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython2.7.so (ver 2.7.6)
--     numpy:                       /usr/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/numpy/core/include (ver 1.8.2)
--     packages path:               lib/python2.7/dist-packages
--
--   Python 3:
--     Interpreter:                 /usr/bin/python3.4 (ver 3.4.3)
--     Libraries:                   /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython3.4m.so (ver 3.4.3)
--     numpy:                       /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages/numpy/core/include (ver 1.8.2)
--     packages path:               lib/python3.4/dist-packages

make
sudo make install

This was shamelessly copied from OpenCV documentation of py setup in Ubuntu.

Q: Where is the post featured image link stored in the WordPress database? A:

Wordpress now has most direct way of getting the featured image url in just one query :

  • PHP: get_the_post_thumbnail_url($post_id, 'full') is the most direct way to retrieve the URL in your theme files.

Q: Issue with Table Reference Formulas in Google Sheets Breaking Table Structure A:

I think this is intentional (albeit undocumented) behaviour, and perhaps a recent change. What appears to be happening when you set a formula in the last row of a table for a column which has not already been autofilled with formulas from the top row, is that Sheets is assuming that you wish the last row of the table to be a footer row (this can be seen from the double line upper border for row 4 in your second screenshot). You then get the #VALUE! error because =table_1[Column 1] is trying to spill an array, but because you are declaring it from the footer row this is not allowed; footer row formulae must include some sort of aggregation so that only a single result is returned (e.g. =sum(table_1[Column 1]) is acceptable).

N.B. =table_1[Column 1] does not give an array result when declared in the body of the table because Sheets uses implicit intersection to return single results corresponding to the appropriate row of the array.

Table footer rows can be referenced using the [#TOTALS] syntax, but I don't recall this being mentioned when Sheets first implemented Tables so this is possibly a new phenomenon. Certainly previously the only way I was aware that footers could be added to Tables was via the older 'Alternating colours' formatting, which Tables still appear to use in the background.
